sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed Monday at 7,619.98, down from a September 3 high of 7,747.71 and sitting near the bottom of its trailing one-month range. The Nasdaq 100 shows the same pattern, off its early-September peak of 29,995 and closing at 29,127. The VIX has drifted up from roughly 14 to 17 over the past two weeks, near the top of its one-month range — a modest pickup in hedging demand, not a spike. The Euro Stoxx 50 sits at its own one-month low, 4.3% off its recent high. The upcoming week carries 6 SP500/R1000/core earnings reports, concentrated in consumer-cyclical, consumer-defensive, industrials and technology names.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: AutoZone reports Tuesday into the consumer-cyclical group, which is tracking a roughly flat median 3-day reaction (-0.2% across 497 tickers). Cintas reports Wednesday into industrials, the softest of this week's represented sectors at -1.5% median across 604 names. Costco reports Thursday into consumer-defensive, also negative at -0.8% median across 362 names. TD Synnex closes out Thursday in technology, the only one of the four sectors sitting positive at +0.7% median across 567 names. Thor Industries (Tue) and General Mills (Wed) round out the week in the same two sectors as AutoZone and Costco.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table this cycle at +6.6% median across 172 tickers, backed by a thick 2,630-item news window. Alternative-asset-management (+2.9%, 6 tickers) and copper (+2.6%, 6 tickers) follow, though both trade on much thinner news flow (232 and 248 items) than mining's coverage. None of this week's SP500/R1000 reporters sit inside these three groups — the events below carry sector tags with flatter recent reaction data instead.
